elements.content: Grammar focus: Verb + Object + Infinitive or Gerund.

Learn each verb with its pattern, then fill the slots in that order: verb, object, complement. Watch the change-of-meaning verbs, where the complement decides the sense: stop to check means pause in order to check, stop checking means no longer check.

verb + object + to-infinitive — persuade, tell, advise, allow: they persuaded the board to delay
verb + object + from + -ing — prevent, stop, discourage: we prevented the error from spreading
verb + object + bare infinitive — perception and let, make, help: I saw them leave
verb + -ing — verbs of liking and avoiding: they avoided signing the deal
verb + to-infinitive — agree, refuse, promise, manage: they refused to sign
change of meaning — remember, stop, try: stop to check and stop checking
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'They persuaded the client ___ the contract.'
2. Complete: 'Nothing will prevent them ___ appealing.'
3. Which pair differs in meaning?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

They asked us to leave. — Verb + object + to-infinitive. (Ask, tell, persuade, advise, encourage.)
They allowed us to stay. — Verb + object + to-infinitive. (Allow, permit, enable.)
They prevented us from staying. — Verb + object + from + -ing. (Prevent, stop, discourage.)
What do you observe?

The main verb decides the complement. Persuade, advise, tell, ask, encourage, allow, permit and enable take an object plus to-infinitive. Prevent, stop, discourage and prohibit take an object plus from + -ing. Verbs of perception (see, hear, watch, notice) take an object plus a bare infinitive or an -ing form, with a difference of completeness: I saw them leave, I saw them leaving.
1. Which pattern follows prevent?
2. What does 'I saw them leave' suggest compared with 'I saw them leaving'?
options: The whole action, start to finish.

elements.content: State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can explain meaning differences.

Success criteria:
- I can use to-infinitive after persuade, allow and advise.
- I can use from + -ing after prevent and discourage.
- I can tell the complete from the progressive action after see and hear.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ They prevented the error to spread (infinitive after prevent) → ✅ They prevented the error from spreading
❌ She advised us waiting (gerund after advise with an object) → ✅ She advised us to wait
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The chair encouraged the team to publish early.
The cost discouraged firms from bidding.
We watched the auditors check every page.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where gerunds and infinitives carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.

Second grammar point of the lesson: Gerunds and Infinitives. Ask what the verb is doing: naming an activity (gerund), pointing at a purpose or a duty (infinitive), or reaching back before the main verb (perfect gerund). After a preposition,
Can you already use this?

- I can use to-infinitive after persuade, allow and advise.
- I can use from + -ing after prevent and discourage.
- I can tell the complete from the progressive action after see and hear.
